judgments.title: Lim Yeong Jer v Tenaga Nasional Berhad
judgments.catchwords: Having reviewed the Record of Appeal, the written submissions and the authorities relied upon, I am satisfied that the Sessions Court’s findings were supported by the evidence and were consistent with the applicable legal principles. The Court’s reasoning demonstrates a proper appreciation of the inspection materials, the statutory presumption under the Electricity Supply Act, and the discovery framework under Order 24 ROC 2012. On the evidence, TNB proved meter tampering and unlawful consumption. The inspection report and photographs, together with the consumption analysis, formed a coherent evidential chain. The Appellant did not produce any expert or documentary evidence capable of undermining TNB’s findings. In accordance with Evergrowth (supra) and Sim Quarry (supra), the statutory presumption was triggered, and the Appellant failed to rebut it with affirmative evidence. The Sessions Court’s refusal of discovery was correct in law. The Appellant did not satisfy the necessity threshold under O.24 r.13, nor did the supporting affidavit comply with the requirements of O.24 r.7(3). The application lacked specificity, did not identify any factual issue requiring determination, and amounted to a speculative attempt to obtain internal TNB materials without demonstrating how such documents were necessary for the fair disposal of the matter. For these reasons, the appeal is dismissed. The Sessions Court’s decision discloses no appealable error, whether of fact, law, or discretion. The findings on tampering, the application of the statutory presumption, and the refusal of discovery are all supported by the record and consistent with the governing authorities. Costs of RM5,000.00 are awarded to the Respondent.
judgments.judge: YA Tuan Nixon Anak Kennedy Kumbong

judgments.catchwords: Offence under section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 read together with section 34 of the Penal Code - Whether the trial judge should have informed at the close of the prosecution's case, that the defence was being called upon to answer a case of actual trafficking or presumed trafficking? - Overwhelming evidence proved the elements of custody, control, and knowledge - Actual possession of the impugned drugs was established - Section 180 (1) and (4) of the Criminal Procedure Code - Procedure after conclusion of case for prosecution - No statutory or legal requirement to state the presumption when calling for the defence - Formal verbal label for an evidentiary rule at the close of the prosecution's case is unnecessary - Statutory presumption of trafficking under section 37(da)(xvi) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 - Section 422 of the Criminal Procedure Code - Not vitiate the conviction - No miscarriage of justice - Failure either to make or to record such a finding does not ipso facto - The law does not require a mini-judgment or detailed legal reasons at the close of the prosecution’s case

judgments.title: SIVACHANDRAN A/L S JAYARAJAH v Pendakwa Raya
judgments.catchwords: Review jurisdiction - Rule 137 of the Rules of the Federal Court 1995 -Inherent powers of Federal Court – All sentences passed to be in accordance with the law – Avoiding miscarriage of justice - Exceptional circumstances - Fresh evidence of prisoner’s death following whipping. Judicial whipping - Corporal punishment - Whether judicial whipping amounts to cruel, inhuman and degrading treatment (“CIDT”) - Whether punishment of whipping is inconsistent with constitutional protection of life, dignity and bodily integrity. Whether whipping is disproportionate and therefore contrary to Article 8(1) - Whether exemption of women from whipping constitutes prohibited discrimination on ground only of gender is contrary to Art 8(2) - Intelligible differentia. Whether whipping is against Art. 5 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (“UDHR”) and the ASEAN Human Rights Declaration in its prohibitions against CIDT - Whether whipping is against customary international law.

judgments.title: Pendakwa Raya v ZAHAR GERALD BIN MEJOH
judgments.catchwords: Undang-undang Perlembagaan - Perlembagaan Persekutuan - Keabsahan Seksyen 12 Akta Senjatapi (Penalti Lebih Berat) 1971 (“FIPA”) - Sama ada Parlimen mempunyai kuasa untuk menggubal undang-undang bagi menghalang Mahkamah daripada menjalankan budi bicara kehakiman untuk membenarkan ikat jamin - Doktrin pengasingan kuasa - Sama ada doktrin pengasingan kuasa merupakan sebahagian daripada asas Perlembagaan - Sama ada terdapat asas bagi menjalankan budi bicara kehakiman berhubung dengan ikat jamin bagi orang yang didakwa atas kesalahan berkaitan senjata api menurut Seksyen 12 FIPA - Hak kesamarataan di sisi undang-undang - Sama ada Seksyen 12 FIPA bertentangan dengan prinsip kesamarataan yang termaktub dalam Perkara 8 Perlembagaan Persekutuan - Maksim “generalia specialibus non derogant” - Sama ada peruntukan berhubung larangan ikat jamin di bawah Seksyen 12 FIPA dimaksudkan untuk mengatasi peruntukan ikat jamin yang bersifat lebih umum menurut Seksyen 388 Kanun Tatacara Jenayah.
